profile.name: Linhan Pang
profile.affiliation: School of Computer Science, Shanghai Jiao Tong University

paragraphs: I am a second-year undergraduate in Computer Science and Technology at the School of Computer Science, Shanghai Jiao Tong University. I joined the university in 2025 and am based in Shanghai, China.

My research interests are machine learning and deep learning, and reinforcement learning. Alongside my studies and research training, I served as a teaching assistant for Python Fundamentals at the 2026 Zhuli Camp and as a student assistant in the Operations Management Office of Academic Affairs.

education.degree: Undergraduate in Computer Science and Technology
education.description: School of Computer Science; second-year undergraduate.

researchInterests.title: Machine Learning and Deep Learning
researchInterests.description: I am interested in how models learn useful representations from data and generalize to new tasks. I hope to explore neural network architectures, optimization, and reliable evaluation, with particular attention to data quality and reproducible experiments.

researchInterests.title: Reinforcement Learning
researchInterests.description: I am interested in how agents learn to make sequential decisions through interaction and feedback. I hope to explore policy learning, exploration, and sample efficiency, as well as applications to autonomous systems and decision-making under uncertainty.

projects.title: AmbiHTMLBench
projects.description: Collect, quality-check and organize data, and contribute to the design of parts of the experimental code framework. The project concerns large language models and machine learning. A submission to ICLR 2027 is planned for September 25, 2026.

projects.title: Summer Research Placement
projects.role: Research Training in Autonomous Driving and Automation
projects.description: Worked on algorithm design and development, system deployment, simulation testing and technical report writing. This placement connected algorithm implementation with system-level experimentation.
